Modern.brandNameRationale: Mysore is the Indian city where Pattabhi Jois developed the Ashtanga self-practice format taught at his Mysore shala from 1948. 'Line' reads as a route, a line of practice, and a clean modern register. Stands at the trade-specific end of yoga naming without using a single Sanskrit syllable.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern yoga studios have split into two cohorts: the boutique-flow brands (Y7, Sky Ting, Loom) and the legacy lineage studios (Jivamukti, Iyengar institutes). The opening is for a modern brand that takes the self-practice (Mysore) format — the room is open, the teacher walks, the practitioner runs their own sequence — and presents it with contemporary studio design.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Sky Ting (skyting.com) holds the design-led modern peer slot in NYC. Y7 Studio (y7-studio.com) plays the flow-led modern middle. Loom Yoga (loomyoga.com) sits in the considered modern peer position. We sit closer to Sky Ting in tone, with a Mysore self-practice format.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern studio for self-practice yoga, on your sequence, with a teacher who walks the room.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Has a daily practice or wants one. Tired of the choreographed flow class. Wants the freedom to run their own sequence.
behaviors: Practices five or more mornings a week

dos: Name the practice in plain language

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — Mysore Line set in a precise modern grotesque, two words on one line, with a thin horizontal underline that reads as the floor of the shala.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Kaivalya is the Sanskrit word from Patanjali's Yoga Sutras meaning 'liberation' or 'aloneness in the absolute' — the final aim of the eight-limb practice. Atelier places the brand in the small-workshop heritage register. The pair reads as a couture yoga house with a serious philosophical anchor.
Luxury.story: Kaivalya Atelier is a small studio in a converted 19th-century townhouse, with a single capped membership and three resident teachers, each with twenty-five-plus years of practice. Practice is by appointment.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury yoga has been dominated by destination retreats (Soulhouse, Sangha) and by city studios with high member fees (Modo, Y7). The opening is for a small couture studio operating in the heritage atelier register — capped membership, named teachers, a single house.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Soulhouse (soulhouse.com) holds the destination luxury peer. Modo Yoga (modoyoga.com) plays the city-luxury peer. The Class (theclass.com) sits in the considered-modern-luxury middle. We sit smaller and more discreet than all of them.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small couture yoga atelier with three resident teachers and capped membership.

targetAudience.primary: 35 to 60. Long-term practitioner. Wants a teacher relationship that lasts decades, not a class pass.

dos: Sign all correspondence by the resident teacher
Print the season's reading list on heavy paper

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Tada — from tadasana, mountain pose, the foundational standing posture. A single syllable, full stop. The brand is the pose: rooted, upright, quiet.
Minimal.industrySummary: Yoga branding has accumulated lifestyle imagery, branded apparel, retreat packages, app subscriptions, and instructional libraries. There's an opening for a brand that strips the whole presentation back to one pose and one teacher.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most yoga apps and studios fail this purity test. The closest peers in spirit are some single-instructor home-practice channels and certain ashtanga-shala self-practice formats.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A yoga practice app. One teacher. One sequence per day. No library.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who already have a practice and want one daily prompt. They will not subscribe to a library.

dos: Show the timer, the breath count, the pose

Minimal.logoDirection: Tada. set in a single-weight grotesque, all lowercase, with a small full stop. The app icon is the wordmark on a soft grey background.

typography.rationale: One family, two weights. The mark and the timer share the same type.

Corporate.tagline: A movement practice institute, professionally run.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (1888–1989) is the documented historical teacher of B.K.S. Iyengar, Pattabhi Jois, T.K.V. Desikachar, and Indra Devi — the lineage from which most modern yoga descends. He is widely referred to as the 'father of modern yoga' in academic literature. Movement Co. signals a serious, institutionally framed corporate operator. The pair reads as a teacher-training and movement-practice institute with academic depth.
Corporate.industrySummary: Yoga teacher training and corporate movement programs have grown into a B2B category alongside the consumer studio market. Buyers are HR teams, hospital systems, sports academies, and large studio groups looking for evidence-based movement curriculum. The opening is an operator anchored in the documented Krishnamacharya lineage rather than a brand-name flow.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Yoga Alliance (yogaalliance.org) holds the certification institutional reference. Yoga Medicine (yogamedicine.com) plays the medical-evidence-led peer. The Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram (kym.org) is the original Chennai institute and historical anchor. We sit closer to Yoga Medicine in operating model, with explicit Krishnamacharya lineage framing.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A movement-practice institute delivering teacher training and clinical movement programs in the documented Krishnamacharya lineage.

targetAudience.primary: Heads of People, hospital wellness directors, sports academy directors, and senior studio operators commissioning teacher training and clinical movement programs.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is a single vertical line with a horizontal bar near the top — the spine in tadasana. Reads cleanly on training certificates, hospital decks, and procurement documents.

Creative.tagline: A yoga studio for the hour you almost skipped.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Breathing Room re-imagines pranayama (the breath-control limb of yoga) as a literal room — the place you go to breathe. The definite article + Room follows the considered-creative naming school (The Wing, The Quiet Room, The Class). Plain, warm, immediately readable.
Creative.manifesto: Most yoga brands sound like a teacher mid-meditation. We sound like the friend who texts 'come, the class starts in twenty minutes, I'll save you a spot.' The brand is warm. The practice is real. The customer gets both.
Creative.industrySummary: Yoga studio branding has been quiet, ethereal, beige, and slightly precious for the last five years. There's room for one that's warm, character-driven, sticker-friendly, and serious about the practice itself.
Creative.competitorLandscape: CorePower (corepoweryoga.com) holds the populist scale slot. Y7 Studio (y7-studio.com) plays the brand-led modern. Sky Ting (skyting.com) sits in the design-led peer position. We sit warmer and more honest than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A yoga studio for the hour you almost skipped.
